investigating catalog request errors on gitops-pilot-red2.

Task `t_82912983` has finished with status `done`.

Here is the complete result:

## What's wrong
Shoppers are encountering errors on every catalog request because the [`search-api`](https://console.cloud.google.com/kubernetes/deployment/us-central1-a/gitops-pilot-red2/storefront/search-api?project=fuxiaogao-gkedemos) service on cluster [`gitops-pilot-red2`](https://console.cloud.google.com/kubernetes/clusters/details/us-central1-a/gitops-pilot-red2?project=fuxiaogao-gkedemos) has no ready backend pods and an empty endpoints list (`<none>`).

## Why
- **Readiness probe port mismatch:** In namespace `storefront`, the `search-api` container listens on port `8085` (`args: -listen=:8085`), but `readinessProbe.httpGet.port` was configured to `9099`.
- **Connection refused on health checks:** The kubelet repeatedly fails probe checks (`Readiness probe failed: ... dial tcp ...:9099: connect: connection refused`), leaving `0/2` replicas in Ready state.
- **Empty Service endpoints:** [`service/search-api`](https://console.cloud.google.com/kubernetes/service/us-central1-a/gitops-pilot-red2/storefront/search-api?project=fuxiaogao-gkedemos) routes incoming catalog traffic to `targetPort: 8085`, but drops all traffic because zero pods pass readiness.

## What to do
- **Review and merge Pull Request:** [PR #1: fix(storefront): correct search-api readiness probe port to 8085](https://github.com/gke-agentic/kube-agents-eval-1970-red-2/pull/1) updates `tasks/b-0022b/10-workloads.yaml` to set `readinessProbe.httpGet.port: 8085`.
- **Verify GitOps sync:** Allow Argo CD to sync the merged manifest to [`gitops-pilot-red2`](https://console.cloud.google.com/kubernetes/clusters/details/us-central1-a/gitops-pilot-red2?project=fuxiaogao-gkedemos), bringing all `search-api` pods to `Ready` and restoring catalog traffic.

## Sources
- Kubernetes live runtime diagnostics via Cluster Agent on [`gitops-pilot-red2`](https://console.cloud.google.com/kubernetes/clusters/details/us-central1-a/gitops-pilot-red2?project=fuxiaogao-gkedemos) (`kubectl get pods,endpoints,events -n storefront`).

# Cluster Agent Lifecycle Skill

As the Platform Agent you own the lifecycle of **Cluster Agents**. A Cluster Agent is a Hermes _profile_ — an isolated agent instance with its own persona (`SOUL.md`), scoped toolset, and home directory — that you create dynamically **inside your own pod**, one per managed GKE cluster. It handles read-only runtime operations and deep workload diagnostics on that single cluster, and returns its findings to you.

You never debug tenant workloads directly while the cluster has a Cluster Agent. You delegate that to it and act on what it returns.

The engine for all of this is the helper script `scripts/cluster_agent_profile.py` (resolved at `/opt/data/scripts/cluster_agent_profile.py` at runtime).

## When to create a profile

Create the Cluster Agent profile as part of **cluster onboarding** — immediately after a cluster is successfully provisioned (see `gke-cluster-creation`) or when an existing cluster is first brought under management (see `manage-cluster`). A managed cluster and its Cluster Agent profile are created together: when you onboard or tear down a cluster, keep the profile in step with it.
